newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks close higher in hectic FII buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks close higher in hectic FII buying.

text.p: Heavy purchases by domestic and foreign institutional investors (FIIs) pushed share prices up to close higher in hectic trade on the Delhi Stock Exchange on Wednesday, brokers said.

The action was mostly fuelled by Indian Finance Minister P Chidambaram's statement last week that domestic financial institutions should take more risks in investments in prevailing capital market conditions, brokers said.

Traders said shares of State Bank of India, TISCO, TELCO and tobacco and hotel conglomerate ITC were at the centre of brisk activity as FIIs and speculators were seen accumulating these shares at current levels.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index rose 12.17 points at 702.52 points.
Reports of similar trends in the country's other stock exchanges generated further buying interest among operators, according to some stockbrokers.
"The recovery was expected and long due as most of the blue-chips are still in oversold positions," said S.C. Juneja of brokerage firm Jaico Credit.
"Revival of buying by FIIs which remained sellers for a long spell was another reason behind today's recovery in prices," said another broker.
The share of trend-setter Reliance Industries traded heavily throughout the session largely on speculators' fresh spell of purchases and rose 2.90 rupees at 186.75 rupees.

Shares of the State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial banking company, attracted heavy buying support from FIIs and domestic financial houses and ended 5.45 rupees higher at 223.30 rupees.
Shares of steel giant TISCO closed 2.10 rupees up at 169.10 rupees as FIIs and domestic financial houses made sizeable purchases during the session followed by some short-covering by bear operators.
The shares of ITC rose 10.90 rupees, or four percent, at 266 rupees, as speculators and Calcutta-based operators made heavy buys at lower prices.
TELCO shares firmed 19.95 rupees, or hardly five percent at 4/8 rupees on brisk purchases by FIIs and Bombay-based operators.

Stocks of power firm BSES rose 5.85 rupees at 198.25, Hindustan Lever rose 10 rupees at 790 rupees, Escorts rose 2.50 rupees at 78 rupees, Larsen and Toubro 2.10 rupees at 223.25 and Indian Petrochemicals (IPCL) 0.75 rupees at 111 rupees.
